title: As-Salam, Peace itself
hookLine: Peace itself, the source of the greeting you've been saying since day one

lines: A NAME PASSING BETWEEN TWO PEOPLE.
cards: As-salamu 'alaykum. You learned it at the very start of this path. Peace be upon you.
It turns up everywhere: at a mosque door, on a phone call, in a shop, shouted across a parking lot. And the answer, wa 'alaykum as-salam, and upon you, peace.
It's said so often it can shrink to a blur, salamlekum, the way good morning becomes morning. But salam isn't only a wish.
As-Salam is one of the most beautiful names, and a saying in al-Bukhari's al-Adab al-Mufrad calls it a name of Allah placed on the earth. So some hear His name passing between two people each time.

teach.b: At the end of al-Hashr, right after the King and the Holy One, Pickthall's translation has a single word: Peace. As-Salam. Its root, s-l-m, means more than quiet: safe, sound, whole, unbroken.
A salim heart is a sound one. Islam, submission, and Muslim come from the same root. So as-Salam is the one who is whole and free from every harm, and the source of every wholeness anyone else has.
Some scholars say the greeting means both: the peace of Allah be on you, and Allah, who is Peace, be with you. Peace wraps the prayer too.
Every prayer ends with as-salamu 'alaykum wa rahmatullah, said with a turn of the head: to the right and then the left, or in one school's practice to the right alone.

teach.h: YOU ARE PEACE, AND FROM YOU IS PEACE.
teach.b: Muslim records that after finishing, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ would say: O Allah, You are Peace, and from You is peace. Blessed are You, Owner of majesty and honor.
The Garden has the same name: in Surah Yunus, Allah calls to dar as-salam, the home of peace. And the Prophet made the greeting a path to love.

In Sahih Muslim he said: you will not enter the Garden until you believe, and you won't believe until you love one another. Shall I tell you something that, if you do it, will make you love one another?
Not a slogan. A practice, for people you know and people you don't.

how: Muslims greet one another with as-salamu 'alaykum and answer wa 'alaykum as-salam; every prayer ends with the greeting of peace and a turn of the head, and after it, following the Prophet's practice, people often say Allahumma anta s-Salam wa minka s-salam.

games.q: the Prophet offers to tell you something that will make people love one another. what is it?
games.why: spread salam among yourselves (Sahih Muslim). the greeting is the practice.

practice: Turn your head gently to the right, as the prayer's closing greeting does, think of someone close, and silently wish them peace, whole and unbroken.
Then turn to the left and think of someone you find difficult, or someone you don't know at all, the cashier, the neighbor, and wish them peace too.
Face forward and let the peace settle in the middle; if you pray, you can say, Allahumma anta s-Salam, O Allah, You are Peace.

wordCard.voice: As-Salam. Peace itself, the whole and the unharmed, the source of all peace, and the first word of the greeting. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Peace, the whole and unharmed; a name of Allah and the first word of the greeting.

carryVoice: Your line: peace is his name. Salaam, peace or a real hello: the wish is the same. Day two hundred forty, done.
